records.name: Books Through Bars
records.summary: A volunteer-run group that sends free books to people in prison who write asking for them. Its office is on Baltimore Avenue in West Philadelphia.
records.what_you_do: Read request letters, pick library books that fit each request, pack and mail the packages, and help with letter logs, donation drives, and library work. New volunteers start at an orientation.

schedule.text: Drop-in volunteer sessions Monday and Thursday from 6:30 to 8:30 pm, and the first Saturday of the month from 11 am to 1 pm. Group sessions are usually Saturdays, 11 am to 1 pm or 1:30 to 3:30 pm, booked in advance.

first_step.how: Fill out the online volunteer form on the volunteer page, pick an orientation, then join a drop-in session
first_step.basis: Built-in newcomer path: a required orientation first, then open drop-in sessions

records.notes: Volunteer page says court-ordered community service volunteers use a separate community service form, which is the basis for court_ordered_ok. Individual and drop-in sessions are for people 18 and older; groups may include under 18s with prior notice. The volunteer page gives an email address for questions (not recorded here). Neither page shows dated news or events, so status is probably_active, not active.

records.name: Speakeasy Open Mic at the Kelly Writers House
records.summary: A monthly open mic at the Kelly Writers House on Penn's campus. Anyone can sign up at the podium for a short slot and read poems, prose, or other short performances.
records.what_you_do: Sign up when you arrive for a three minute slot and perform, or come to listen and take part in the room.

schedule.text: Monthly open mic, in person. The next listed session is Wednesday, October 28, 2026 at 7 pm.

first_step.how: Come in person and sign up at the podium when you arrive. Each slot is three minutes. No advance registration is listed.
first_step.basis: Explicitly open to anyone with a set way in: sign up on arrival for a short slot

records.notes: The calendar lists the October 28, 2026 session as in person and welcoming all kinds of performances. The day of the month has varied: a 2023 guide said first Wednesday, while the 2026 listings fall on fourth Wednesdays. Cost is not listed on current pages. The sign-up details come from the August 20, 2026 special edition page for the incoming class, so treat them as the usual pattern, not a confirmed rule.

records.name: The Poets' Studio at Twelve Gates Arts
records.summary: A monthly gathering for Philadelphia poets. Each session has a featured poet who reads and then leads a writing workshop. It is free and open to anyone interested in writing.
records.what_you_do: Hear the featured poet read, then join a hands-on writing workshop with other poets.

schedule.text: Monthly evening session, 7 to 8:30 pm. The June 2026 session was on a Tuesday.

first_step.how: Register for a session through the event's ticket link (Eventbrite), or come to the free session
first_step.basis: Open to the public with a clear registration link; the page does not name a beginner track

records.notes: The event page header says June 9, 2026, but its description says February 9th, 2026. Confirm the date before attending. No dedicated series page is linked; the series name comes from the event page. The page does not state whether the session is recurring every month, so confirm with the organizer.

records.name: A Novel Idea book clubs
records.summary: A bookstore on East Passyunk that runs book clubs on set dates. Two were listed for October 2026: a myth and legend club and a fiction club.
records.what_you_do: Read the listed book and meet at the store to talk about it with other readers.

schedule.text: Dated sessions on the store's site: Myth and Legend Book Club on October 8, 2026 at 6 pm, and Fiction Book Club on October 29, 2026 at 6:30 pm.

cost.text: The site lists $30.00 and $27.99 next to the club dates. It does not say whether these are book prices or fees.

first_step.how: Check the store's site for the club date and get the listed book. The site does not say how to join.
first_step.basis: Dated sessions are listed, but the site does not say how to join or whether the clubs are open to the public

records.notes: Hours on the store site run Wednesday to Sunday. The site does not say whether the clubs are open to the public, how members join, or what the listed prices cover. Billy Penn (Feb 2026) says the store hosts two monthly book clubs, which matches the site.

records.name: The Blue Stoop
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit for local writers. It offers free drop-in writing time, free skill-share sessions on Zoom, and classes in poetry, fiction, memoir, and other forms, with financial aid offered.
records.what_you_do: Join a free drop-in writing session, attend a free skill share, or take a multi-week class with other writers.

schedule.text: Creative Coworking drop-in on Zoom on Wednesdays, 3:30 to 5:30 pm. Thursdays on the Stoop free Zoom skill shares, 4 to 5 pm. Most classes meet weekday evenings, 6:30 to 8:30 pm, for 6 to 9 weeks.

locations.label: Zoom, plus partner venues across Philadelphia

cost.text: Drop-in sessions and skill shares are free. Class tuition is not shown on the page; financial aid is offered.

first_step.how: Use the registration link for a free Creative Coworking or Thursdays on the Stoop session. The link sends the Zoom details.
first_step.basis: Free sessions are open to all and have a clear RSVP, but the page names no beginner track

records.notes: The events page is very long. Only the first 100,000 characters were read, so later listings were not seen. Dated items seen: an in-person session on October 6, a workshop with Philadelphia poet laureate Raina J. Leon on October 25, and a Zoom coworking session on December 9, 2026.

records.name: Adult Education Philadelphia (volunteer tutors)
records.summary: The city's adult education program, run with community partners. It trains volunteer tutors to help adults build reading, writing, math, computer, and English skills.
records.what_you_do: Tutors work one-on-one with a learner or serve as classroom aides in reading, writing, math, basic computer skills, or English. Tutors take a free training before they are matched with a learner.

schedule.text: Free tutor training of about 10 to 12 hours, completed before a learner match. Tutoring times are set with each learner.

first_step.how: Apply through the online volunteer form linked on the city page. Questions go to adultedu@phila.gov.
first_step.basis: Clear public application path, and training is provided before matching

records.notes: The city page does not state the tutor time commitment, age minimum, or background check rules for tutors. Idealist listings (lead source only, posted Dec 2025) say 2 to 4 hours a week for 3 to 6 months, age 18 and up, and a background check, but these were not verified on the city page. The learner enrollment hotline, (833) 750-5627, is for learners, not tutor sign-up. Dated items on the page: August 13 and August 26, 2026.

records.name: Drexel Late Night Series
records.summary: A free weekly open mic night at Drexel's Creese Commuter Lounge, run by Drexel students. Performers sign up for five-minute slots in music, comedy, poetry, or monologues.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a five-minute slot and perform, or come to watch the show.

schedule.text: Every Thursday. Sign-ups open at 7:30 pm for the 8 pm show.

first_step.how: Sign up for a five-minute slot at the lounge from 7:30 pm on a Thursday
first_step.basis: Anyone interested can claim a slot; the page names no beginner track

records.notes: The page has no dated items, and the footer copyright year is not evidence. A 2023 Billy Penn guide also lists the Thursday schedule, which supports it. The venue is given only by cross streets.

records.name: The Soapbox: Community Print Shop and Zine Library
records.summary: A print shop and zine library in West Philadelphia with public open hours on Wednesday evenings and Sunday afternoons. Members use the presses, and the studio teaches printmaking, bookmaking, and zine making.
records.what_you_do: Browse the zine library, take a printmaking or zine workshop, or join as a member to use the presses.

schedule.text: Public open hours: Wednesdays 6 to 10 pm and Sundays 1 to 5 pm. Members have their own access times.

cost.text: Membership plans and workshops charge fees. The site lists no prices.

first_step.how: Visit during public open hours (Wednesday evenings or Sunday afternoons), or ask about membership or a workshop through the studio's site
first_step.basis: Public open hours are posted; the site does not describe a newcomer program

records.notes: The studio's own site gives 4700 Kingsessing Ave and public open hours, but no dated events, prices, or membership tiers. A late 2025 announcement seen in search results (not opened) said the studio would move to 4542 Baltimore Ave in spring 2026. Check the address before visiting. The site does not say whether the zine library is open to non-members during open hours. Library size varies by source (1,200 to 3,500), so no count is recorded.

records.name: Mad Poets Society
records.notes: The events page shows no dated events and no Philadelphia service statement. Revisit if the group starts serving Philadelphia.

notes: Searches: all 10 used (cap reached). Fetches: 24, including the 404s. Verdicts: 8 publish, 1 out_of_area (Mad Poets Society). Thrillerdelphia and Cupid's Bookshop were not published: their store sites showed no book club details, so their clubs stay leads. Silent Book Club Philadelphia has no 2025 or 2026 evidence. Gaps: no affinity book clubs (LGBTQ, Black, Latino) turned up in search, and no adult literacy tutoring program other than the city's. The Free Library site was not opened, so its programs are leads only. Names with no URL found and kept here only: East Falls Zine Reading Room (a cataloged collection of over 1,600 zines run by two people), Little Berlin (a Kensington artist collective whose zine library went to Temple), Consonant Collective (zines and records), the Pennsylvania Prison Society arts program, Prison Literacy Project of Pennsylvania, and Lifers, Inc. (named in 2013 to 2021 coverage, not checked). Philly Queer Zine Fest was a one-time June 2025 event at Penn. Not included as groups: the Rosenbach's Sherlock Mondays (a virtual talk series) and WXPN's LIVE at the Writers House (a radio recording with RSVP seats). The Idealist city tutor listing is lead-only and was used only for the notes above. Eventbrite, Meetup, and Facebook were not read beyond search listings. The Blue Stoop record reads only the first 100,000 characters of a long events page.
